title: The Five-Minute Workout
scene: You decide to squeeze in a five-minute workout before breakfast because it sounds almost too easy to fail. The instructor, your body, and finally your watch each have slightly different opinions about how well that plan is going.
sceneJa: 朝食前に5分だけ運動することにする。簡単そうに見えたが、インストラクター、自分の体、そして最後には腕時計まで、それぞれ違う評価を下してくる。

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: Five minutes sounded perfectly manageable / which is an attractive phrase / when you are still lying in bed
Five minutes / sounded perfectly / manageable which is an attractive phrase
Five minutes sounded / perfectly manageable which / is an attractive phrase when
questions.explanation: The first chunk gives the speaker’s judgment, the next comments on that judgment, and the final chunk adds the situation in which it sounds attractive.

questions.question: What does ‘I began to question’ mean here?
options: I started to doubt whether the description was reasonable
I began asking the instructor personal questions
I stopped doing the workout immediately
questions.explanation: The speaker starts doubting the instructor’s use of the word ‘gentle’ because the workout feels much harder than expected.

questions.question: Why is ‘I decided not to argue’ funny here?
options: The watch can actually debate with the speaker
The speaker treats the watch’s disappointing judgment as if it were an authority worth arguing with
The instructor asked the speaker to remain silent
questions.explanation: The humour comes from calmly accepting the watch’s judgment and pretending it has done better research than the speaker.

speak: Begin with mild optimism and keep the tone conversational. Let the disbelief grow slightly at ‘gentle but effective’ and ‘properly warmed up.’ Deliver ‘I was nearly dead’ without exaggerating it. Slow down for the final two lines and sound almost respectfully defeated by the watch; the dry humour works best when the punchline is understated.
review: Today’s flow: sensible plan → confident start → unexpectedly hard reality → small victory → external judgment → dry surrender. Key expressions: ‘perfectly manageable’ for something that seems easy enough, ‘begin to question’ for growing doubt, and ‘decide not to argue’ as a dry way to accept reality.
